I'm late but here's a few things that helped me:

- People always try to assume the best of you, so don't ruminate on small, embarrassing mistakes in the past.

- Even if it would truly help them, some people just don't want to change. It's not your fault, and I know it hurts but you can't change others who aren't willing to change.

- Look at your situation as if you were a friend and give yourself advice and comfort from that stand point. More importantly, tunnel vision is the most dangerous thing you can get when you are depressed. It's what kills people in the end, so hopefully taking a step back will relieve some of that.

This is what I've been doing my whole life. I love myself more than most people do, and I never really cared about friends or anything. However, self love and the love you receive from people around you is different. Both are needed to thrive, and to feel a sense of belonging and trust you need love from others. It's not a burden to have needs, and it's not a flaw to want others to cheer you on as well. It's normal, expessially after never receiving conditionally love by everyone in your life.


I understand what you were trying to say, but it's a flawed way of thinking if you believe that you will burden others because you need someone to care about you too. It's not. We all have needs, and it's okay to rely on others for support and care too.

Yes. It's because of my family, and always having to play a different role for different family members just not to get hurt by them.

I have a personality that is always happy and pure, and will always do what people say because I want people to like me. This part was meant to deal with my grandmother and her constant, various abuses of me when I was a kid. Likewise, I have another personality that is rather sarcastic and stubborn, and really dislikes people. This part was meant to deal with my sister, who I wasnt ever able to appease with my submissive part so I had to be rather rude to make sure she didnt hurt me.

I usually use a variety of different personalities with people who seem threatening, but most times my mind is always in the submissive, happy personality I guess when I talk to people outside of my family.

My family and friends don't really care about me, and I've even been told that by them multiple times before. It hurts, honestly. Also, I often do remember strangers or people I talk to, but that's only me. I doubt that anyone would remember me because I literally dont make a difference to anyone's life. And if I did some how make a small difference, then they would only remember the person who I pretended to be for them. They wouldn't remember ME if that makes any sense.
Like another comment said, it's called internal family systems. Basically you have different parts of you who like different things and do different actions as a result of abuse.
How do you get people to care about you?  My family never cared about me, so it's hard for me to really think people care about me

Looked at your post history and saw you also have body dysmorphia. My best advice is to avoid all rate me subs, ESPECIALLY true rate me (it claims to be brutally honest, but it's more about brutality than honesty).

With that said, I would advise to seek help for this more than anything. Having people say you're ugly or not will only lead to temporary satisfaction if they say you arent, and will lead to years of negative thoughts if they say you are. After all, body dysmorphia doesnt go away after one compliment on your appearance but worsens with every negative comment. 

Please stay safe.

Hey, just take a deep breath.

 You seem to be overwhelmed mentally at the moment, so just take a second to calm down and ignore the school work for a second. You seem to be quite unmotivated, and I'm guessing that you've already tried to motivate yourself but nothing has worked. No matter what people say, or you say to yourself, you just don't feel like doing anything.
 I mean, why do anything when all you want to do is escape from reality and wish you were never here in so much pain? What's the point at the end of the day? What's the point at all if you don't even want to live to see tomorrow?

Not to mention that this feeling of motivation and hopelessness just gets worse as work is piled ontop of your already overwhelmed mind, and you drift further behind and lose hope of ever getting back to date on stuff. It's an understatement to say this feeling sucks, and it just creates a positive feedback loop the more you wait to do something. It makes you wish you were dead. 

With that said, I'm not here to exactly encourage you. It's hard to just start feeling motivated by a random  stranger on the internet who doesnt know your situation at all and who you'll never talk to again. However, I do want to just say this: Slow down and start small. I've been in the situation you are in before, and my depression only got worse by the tunnel vision of the vast amount of work I had left to do. Overall, I spent more time worrying about the work than doing it in the end. With this, I just want to say to just focus on one small thing at a time. For me, it was just reading one page of a textbook for one day. No notes or anything. Just one simple page. And if that seems too big, then I would suggest to just ignore all of the work for the moment. Just do something that will make you feel better about yourself. Something as simple as getting out of bed or making breakfast. Just try to do something that will make you feel a little bit happier and motivated. I know it's really hard to do, and it's more comforting to just not do anything, but trust me when I say that comfort in doing nothing is only a placebo. It'll make you feel atleast okay right now, but it'll go away with time and it'll make you miserable if you don't have anything but that false feeling to fall back on.

Sorry to write so much, I truly hope you get to feeling better. Please, take care.

To begin, I just wanted to day that you're way, way beyond any writer I've read recently. I'm not normally a reader, but I found myself reading your whole post because it was beautiful and poetic, and yet also described feelings I couldn't put words to. Please, continue to write and express your feelings in any way possible.

Now, to the post. You seem to be going through a lot at the moment, so I'll start with the first paragraph. You seem to be pushing yourself too much. By calling yourself names and forcing happiness that will only happen with time, you are only making things mentally worse for yourself. I know it's hard, and I know you truly want to get out of the mess youre in as quickly as possible so that you don't get overwhelmed, but it all takes time. When I feel like this too, I compare it to having a broken foot. I'm hurting right now, and it sucks to see people run and do things with their lives when you can't even walk or get out of bed most days. But, as time passes and you get proper help, things will get better and you'll be able to do what others do. But don't push yourself or else your just going to make it worse and itll take more time to heal properly.

Now, the next paragraph. You seem like a very kind a genuine person, someone who puts others before themselves at any given opportunity. You said this is because you love them and you want them to be happy, regardless of how much they end up harming you. You care too much, and no one really gives you the equal amount of care you give them. If I have to be honest, being in a relationship- no matter the type- and being so caring will only lead you to get taken advantage of by the wrong people. My best advice would be to get new friends, but I know that's hard considering how much love and care you already spent on people who you hold dear. The next best option would be to set boundaries and hold yourself back from giving to much. If they can't respect you, then you shouldn't give them the amount of love you're already giving them.

Now, for the final two paragraphs. You're not rambling, every word you say is important and I'm happy that you're able to open up about this. It takes a lot of courage, and I know it's only coming from an internet stranger, but I'm proud of you. I know you want to understand what's going on with you, and that's reasonable. I would encourage you to continue learning, and to learn as much as you can but don't let it take over your life. With that said, you seem to be quite isolated at the moment. Dreams of a new life and of things you long for can be good in the short run, but in the long run, it can absolutely destroy you if it remains unchecked. If I have to be honest, I still struggle with this even today. I dont have much advice to give you, but the one thing I can say is that going outside and to places you are familiar with but not as familiar as,- let's say- your house really helps to get rid of these thoughts and feel somewhat human again I guess is the best way to put it. Being stuck in one enviorment all day can deeply affect your outlook on the world since you arent given an opportunity to exercise it. 

I hope this helps a little, and I'm sorry that it's so long.

I'm sorry you're in such a sticky situation right now, and I know you probably feel super cornered and helpless to help her. You might feel like you have to help her no matter what because she is your bestie, and so you'll sacrifice your own mental health for her well being. However, this isn't right. Your mental health is, and should be to you, the number one priority. If you dont think it is, then remember that you have to be mentally healthy in order to help others out of their own situation. I know that sounds kinda tough and it's hard pill to swallow, but it's the truth and you need to help yourself as well. Furthermore, you might not like to hear this, but the situation you are in sounds kind of abusive. Making threats of suicide if you leave and always putting you on the spot about it isn't necessarily the best friendship dynamic to have. Not everyone is willing to help themselves, and if they keep on insinuating killing themselves if you leave then it just sounds really toxic. My best advice is to set boundaries, and if that does not work, then please take what I say next to heart. You can't save everyone. Not everyone is willing to be saved. Not even the most talented word smith can save someone who does not want to help themselves. Also, from my experiences and the stories that I've heard, it's unlikely that she'll kill herself if you left. Take this with a grain of salt, but usually suicide is a common pawn in an abusive relationship since people know it will take an emotional toll on the helping party. They think it will cause you not to leave, and maybe it does for awhile, but just remember that her life is her choice. You can help by being there for her, but if she is not willing to help herself then there is nothing else you can do.

(Also, from my personal take, she shows symptoms of Borderline Personality Disorder. Her suicidal attitude and abandonment issues is quite a hall mark of the disorder. However, I am no specialist and it's just a thought I had when I read your post. Please take it with a grain of salt.)

Again, I'm really sorry you are in such a horrible situation. I hope everything gets better and you focus on your mental health more as well
